name: Mythic Europe
description: The setting of Ars Magica, ruled by a noble warrior caste in the thirteenth century.

name: Order of Hermes
description: The mysterious Order of magicians lurking at the edges of noble society, forbidden to meddle in mundane affairs.

name: The Church
description: A major landholder throughout Mythic Europe whose allies, excommunication, and interdiction shape noble politics.

name: Realms of Power
description: The four Realms, against which a realistic mundane world can be contrasted in sagas.

name: Gratitude
description: A structured advancement system in which characters earn Gratitude points for exceptional service to their lord, redeemed for office, land, or goods.

name: Advancement Requirements Table
description: Table listing the Gratitude, abilities, and costs required to rise from serf to freeman, warrior to knight, and through noble offices.

name: Patron
description: Virtue representing a close relationship with a friendly lord, letting the character influence how Gratitude is expressed.

name: Landed Noble
description: Virtue gained by a character raised to hold land; grants 12 points of agents and is a Major Social Virtue.

name: Greater Noble
description: Virtue suited to a character given high noble office.

name: Temporal Influence
description: Virtue needed by characters designed as officers of a lord.

name: Heir
description: Virtue representing expectation of inheritance; a variant applies to younger sons sheltered after lost causes.

name: Social Contacts
description: Virtue granting 12 points on the Agent Recruitment Table for thematically appropriate agents.

name: Mercenary Captain
description: Minor Social Virtue that grants agents at character creation and requires underlings.

name: Close Family Ties
description: Virtue granting agents at character creation.

name: Magister in Artibus
description: Major Social Virtue with agent resistance 3.

name: Redcap
description: Listed as a Major Social Virtue on the Agent Recruitment Table.

name: Custos
description: Covenant guard; a Minor Social Virtue. Covenants raise unwanted children as custodes.

name: Clerk
description: Minor Social Virtue; clerks are employed by nobles to write letters and are often priests.

name: Failed Apprentice
description: Minor Social Virtue on the Agent Recruitment Table.

name: Gentleman/woman
description: Minor Social Virtue on the Agent Recruitment Table.

name: Mendicant Friar
description: Minor Social Virtue on the Agent Recruitment Table.

name: Priest
description: Minor Social Virtue; priests serve in noble households as clerks and chancellors.

name: Wise One
description: Minor Social Virtue on the Agent Recruitment Table.

name: Covenfolk
description: Free Social Virtue with agent resistance 0.

name: Craftsman
description: Free Social Virtue with agent resistance 0.

name: Merchant
description: Free Social Virtue with agent resistance 0.

name: Peasant
description: Free Social Virtue; peasants provide food, labor, and soldiers for the nobility.

name: Wanderer
description: Free Social Virtue with agent resistance 0.

name: Hermetic Magus
description: Free Social Virtue excluded from the Agent Recruitment Table; Hermetic magi cannot be agents.

name: Gossip
description: Minor General Virtue adding +1 to an agent's resistance.

name: Magic Sensitivity
description: Minor Supernatural Virtue adding +1 to an agent's resistance.

name: Protection
description: Minor Virtue adding +1 to an agent's resistance.

name: Skinchanger
description: Minor Supernatural Virtue adding +1 to an agent's resistance.

name: Entrancement
description: Major Supernatural Virtue adding +3 to an agent's resistance.

name: True Faith
description: Major Virtue adding +3 to an agent's resistance.

name: Wealthy
description: Major General Virtue adding +3 to an agent's resistance.

name: Faerie Friend
description: Listed among useful traits that add +1 to an agent's resistance.

name: Magical Animal Companion
description: Listed among useful traits that add +1 to an agent's resistance.

name: Dark Secret
description: Story Flaw; can arise from hidden bastards or younger sons wanted by authorities, and can be forged by intriguers.

name: Story Flaw
description: Category of Flaw that intriguers can uncover; agents dominated by coercion have one.

name: Difficult Underlings
description: Flaw gained when a principal controls an agent who considers him a social inferior or hates him.

name: Blackmail
description: Story Flaw representing an agent's attempt to shed a principal's control, or leverage used to dominate an agent.

name: Enemies
description: Major Flaw likely to inconvenience a principal (-3 to agent resistance).

name: Feud
description: Major Flaw likely to inconvenience a principal.

name: Lycanthrope
description: Major Flaw likely to inconvenience a principal.

name: Plagued By Supernatural Entity
description: Major Flaw likely to inconvenience a principal.

name: Black Sheep
description: Minor Flaw likely to inconvenience a principal.

name: Dependent
description: Minor Flaw; a hostage dependent may be used to dominate an agent.

name: Diabolic Past
description: Minor Flaw that can inconvenience a principal or be used as blackmail leverage.

name: Favors
description: Minor Flaw likely to inconvenience a principal.

name: Infamous
description: Minor Flaw likely to inconvenience a principal.

name: True Love
description: Minor Flaw; a beloved may be held hostage to dominate an agent.

name: Branded Criminal
description: Minor Social Flaw with agent resistance -1.

name: Outcast
description: Minor Social Flaw with agent resistance -1.

name: Outlaw Leader
description: Minor Social Flaw that requires underlings.

name: Outlaw
description: Major Social Flaw with agent resistance -3.

name: Outsider
description: Major Social Flaw with agent resistance -3.

name: Busybody
description: Useful Minor Flaw adding +1 to agent resistance.

name: Mentor
description: Useful Minor Flaw adding +1 to agent resistance.

name: Blatant Gift
description: Form of the Gift that makes ordinary people like merchants reluctant to deal with a magus.

name: The Gift
description: Magical talent whose social penalty is subtracted from Leadership and agent-control rolls.

name: Leadership
description: Ability required for offices like admiral and marshal and used to control agents and affinity.

name: Profession: Steward
description: Ability required for butler, steward, and treasurer offices.

name: Church Lore
description: Ability usually held by a chancellor.

name: Intrigue
description: Ability used to hire criminals, uncover information, spread rumors, and gauge class opinion.

name: Charm
description: Social ability usable when persuading agents to perform tasks.

name: Stealth
description: Ability used by saboteurs against sentries.

name: Awareness
description: Ability used by sentries to detect saboteurs.

name: Reputation
description: A character's standing, used to judge the interests of nobles and affected by deeds, rumors, and treatment of lords.

name: Noble Reputation
description: A fourth style of Reputation alongside Local, Hermetic, and Ecclesiastic, allowing members of the landed class to know about each other.

name: Prudhomme
description: The prize reputation for a male noble: a man tested and found sound, noble of blood, handsome, prowess in war, and suitable character.

name: Affinity
description: The coalition of allied landholders around a magnate's demesne; also a bonus to social Ability rolls in a region.

name: Caput
description: The core lands at the center of a nobleman's affinity in England and France.

name: Agents
description: Directly controlled subordinates bound to a principal by emotional Bonds, limited in number by Presence and Intrigue or Leadership.

name: Factor
description: Hermetic term for a primary agent through whom a principal controls a network.

name: Bond
description: A Personality Trait expressing why and how strongly an agent is attached to a principal.

name: Agency Experience
description: Experience points earned alongside Adventure Experience, spent to recruit agents and maintain Bonds.

name: Agent Recruitment Table
description: Table giving the resistance of potential agents by social status, flaws, and resources.

name: Mesnie
description: The household knights of a lord, fed, clothed, and equipped by him and expected to be loyal.

name: Mesnie privée
description: A select group of friends of a powerful lord within his mesnie who strongly reflect his tastes.

name: Bacheler
description: A member of a lord's mesnie; the title shows the knight has a patron.

name: Carissimus
description: The captain of a mesnie, the lord's best friend or most skilled knight.

name: Knight
description: Mounted warrior of the noble class; also a Minor Social Virtue.

name: Squire
description: A youth serving a knight who mentors him in the arts of war.

name: Banneret
description: A landed noble with enough wealth to hire knights, usually from five manors.

name: Baron
description: A noble title above banneret; a greater baron has an Affinity bonus of +4.

name: Earl
description: Senior noble of a shire whose household averages 140 people.

name: Magnate
description: Great noble with a sphere of influence, retinue, tenants, and affinity.

name: Admiral
description: Officer who finds, provisions, crews, and commands a lord's vessels of war.

name: Butler
description: Nominally the king's wine steward, responsible for feeding the court.

name: Chancellor
description: Master of the king's correspondence and chief advisor on foreign relations and the Church, almost always a priest.

name: Chamberlain
description: Officer responsible for the king's chamber, retinue, and personal possessions.

name: Constable
description: Royal officer title; in France the Constable leads the army and may countermand the king in battle.

name: Counselor
description: A person who gives useful advice in the lord's select councils.

name: Justiciar
description: The king's primary officer for enforcing law, often acting as regent.

name: Marshal
description: Leader of the king's bodyguard and of the royal army in the field.

name: Sheriff
description: Nobleman who pays the king for the right to collect royal revenues in a shire; equivalents are bailie, sénéchal, and vogt.

name: Steward
description: Officer responsible for all parts of the court not assigned to others; often a woman.

name: Treasurer
description: Guardian of the lord's wealth and treasury.

name: Coroner
description: English office of four elected knights per shire who curb sheriffs, collect royal rights, and collect murdrum.

name: Forest Warden
description: Noble officer administering the king's forests, served by rangers and surveyors.

name: Verderer
description: Unpaid landowners appointed to track fines taken by forest wardens.

name: Regarder
description: Knights appointed every third year to census threats to forest animals.

name: Agistor
description: Knights guarding the king's rights over animals pastured in the forest.

name: Chancery
description: The clerical section of a large estate's household.

name: Primogeniture
description: Inheritance by the eldest son, now accepted for the thrones of England and France.

name: Appanage
description: Non-heritable sections of an estate given to younger sons for their lifetime.

name: Dowry
description: Money or goods paid by the bride's family to the bride upon marriage.

name: Dower
description: Payment by a husband's family to an heiress's father or guardian.

name: Relief
description: The largest vassal tax, levied on inherited land.

name: Aids
description: Taxes owed to a lord, theoretically voluntary gifts, for knighting, marriage, or ransom.

name: Levy
description: Peasant warriors mustered by vassals.

name: Scutage
description: A fine paid instead of sending knights to war, usually two pounds per knight in England.

name: Wardship
description: A liege's right over the lands and marriage of heirs and widows of his vassals.

name: Disparagement
description: Illegal selling of a ward's marriage or marriage to unsuitable persons.

name: Excommunication
description: The Church's most powerful weapon, forbidding Christians to deal with the excommunicant.

name: Interdiction
description: Forbidding Church services in all of a nobleman's lands.

name: Amercement
description: A fine negotiated with a judge to avoid gruesome physical punishment.

name: Murdrum
description: A fine on a community where a secretly killed person cannot be proven English rather than Norman.

name: Deodand
description: An object that has killed a person, collected by the coroner.

name: Treasure Trove
description: Valuable buried objects collected by the coroner.

name: Abjuring the Realm
description: Process by which a felon in sanctuary confesses, forfeits goods, and leaves the realm.

name: Royal Forest
description: In England, a legal term for areas declared the king's sole hunting preserves.

name: Vassalage
description: Feudal bond between lord and vassal providing resources, advice, and warriors.

name: Subinfeudation
description: Nobles holding land from multiple lieges.

name: Benefice
description: A Church office with income in the gift of a lord.

name: Crusade
description: Warfare in distant lands, granting Reputation.

name: Black Mass
description: A diabolical rite that adds to a character's Reputation.

name: Code of Hermes
description: The law of the Order; covenants outbidding nobles for sheriff roles likely breaches it.

name: Quaesitores
description: Hermetic investigators who judge breaches of the Code.

name: House Tytalus
description: Hermetic House seeking to run a case in a mortal court.

name: Covenant
description: A community of magi that nobles may serve or that raise custodes.

name: Might
description: Supernatural creatures' score affecting reputation experience from study.

name: Faerie
description: Supernatural beings that may cause strife and answer human desires.

name: Demon
description: Infernal being that may foster lies to cause strife.

name: Dark Faerie
description: A faerie that leaves faerie-wrought weapons for a lost heir.

name: Ghost
description: Spirit of a murder victim that may haunt killers.

name: Dragon
description: Creature scared off by a clever ruse.

name: Greek Fire
description: Weapon of Byzantine galleys used to destroy ships.

name: Normans
description: Invaders of England whose culture favors primogeniture.

name: Robert the Bruce
description: Historical figure whose birth inspires a story seed.

name: Thomas Becket
description: Archbishop of Canterbury whose mesnie deserted him.

name: King John
description: King of England who preferred being excommunicant.

name: King Richard
description: King whose forest law punished deer poachers.

name: Philip Augustus
description: The current king of France.

name: William the Conqueror
description: Norman who divided England's lands.

name: Henry II of England
description: King who claimed descent from Satan.

name: Satan
description: The Devil, claimed as ancestor by Henry II.

name: Duke Simon
description: Example noble with many vassals.

name: Matthew
description: Young landed knight, Simon's vassal.

name: Benedict
description: Bishop grateful to Duke Simon.

name: Lord Corvinius
description: Example lord.

name: Count of Champagne
description: Example liege.

name: England
description: Kingdom with coroners, forest law, and scutage.

name: France
description: Kingdom with appanage and constables.

name: Italy
description: Region with dowry customs.

name: Catalonia
description: Region where bequests to daughters are illegal.

name: Sicily
description: Kingdom where vassals serve 60 days.

name: Byzantium
description: Empire whose galleys use Greek fire.

name: Scotland
description: Country with English offices.

name: Ireland
description: Partly English-dominated country.

name: Wales
description: Partly English-dominated country.

name: The Marches
description: Area where judicial rights are delegated to nobles.

name: Canterbury
description: Archbishopric of Thomas Becket.

name: Holy Land
description: Object of the Crusades.

name: Hell
description: Damnation for excommunicants.

name: Battle of Grissors
description: Battle where English spears turned French cavalry.
